rich_summary: Arjuna battles the aged king Bhagadatta, who fights from his massive war elephant and showers Arjuna and Krishna with weapons. Arjuna skillfully destroys Bhagadatta’s bow, armor, and missiles, wounding the elephant and pressing the attack. In desperation, Bhagadatta invokes the infallible Vaishnava weapon and hurls it at Arjuna, but Krishna steps in front of the hero and receives it on his own chest, where it harmlessly turns into a garland. Arjuna questions why Krishna broke his vow not to fight, and Krishna reveals the ancient origin of the weapon, once granted to Naraka and passed down to Bhagadatta. With the threat removed, Arjuna kills the elephant and then Bhagadatta. The episode highlights Krishna’s divine nature and protective role, while confirming Arjuna as the decisive warrior on the battlefield.

highlight_spans.why: Opens the scene with Arjuna and Krishna together on the chariot as Bhagadatta begins the fierce assault.
The crucial moment when Bhagadatta launches the Vaishnava weapon and Krishna receives it on his chest, transforming it into a garland.
Krishna explains his four cosmic forms and the ancient history of the Vaishnava weapon, revealing his divine role in protecting the world.
Arjuna fires the decisive arrow that strikes between the elephant’s frontal globes, a dramatic turning point in the duel.
The death of Bhagadatta, described with vivid imagery as he falls from his elephant like a flower torn from its stem.

top_scenes.scene_text: Krishna standing before Arjuna on the chariot as the blazing Vaishnava weapon strikes his chest and transforms into a radiant garland.
Arjuna releasing a powerful arrow that crashes into the armored war elephant’s forehead while Bhagadatta struggles to control it.
Bhagadatta falling from his golden-armored elephant after Arjuna’s final arrow pierces his chest amid the chaos of battle.
